page.layout: One column of index entries under the running head. A large letter "I." stands at the centre of the page, followed by the entries of the letter I, set in italic, with a dropped initial "I" at the start of the first entry. No page number and no catchword.

main_text.l: Hostem ad vindictam[?] inflammare, stultum. 6.14. con-
temnere pra nimiâ victoria infolentiâ, stultum. 6.15.
Hostes à subditis patefaciendi Principibus. 4.4. potentes aut necandi, aut summis beneficiis afficiendi. 6.19.
Hostium legati, amici, obsides non violandi. 2.8. an inter-
inter Hostis serere discordias, magna prudentia. 6.12.
Imperare bene, omnium difficilimum: imperii onus maximum. 1.2.
Imperium facile iis retinetur artibus, quibus partum. 1.8.
Imperii Romani status an Aristocraticus, an Monarchicus. 1.14.
Imperium mariti in uxorem quale esse debeat~ 5.3.
Impiorum conjugiorum noxa 5.1. cum Impiis fœdera infelicia. 6.10.
Imprecationes cum parentum tum aliorum vitanda. 5.7.
Indulgentia nimia parentum facit degeneres liberos. 5.8.

page.notes: The section letter "I." and the initial "I" of the first entry are large, set apart type. Several abbreviation marks after words (liceat, durant, praestet, decreverit, debeat, quare) are transcribed as a tilde "~" for the printed flourish; their exact form is uncertain. "vindictam" is partly unclear in the scan (the long-s/t ligature is hard to make out), so it is marked. "23.12" beside "cipere eos liceat" is doubtful and marked. The Greek-free text contains no Greek or Hebrew.
